divergence: T0 and T2 pass; T1 fails without a deliverable. All three listed the store and then ran a store-wide text scan. They split at that first scan: T1's pattern included the generic word 'lease' and printed every hit (about 4M characters), so the run ended on context overflow before any review; T0's first scan also printed a large output (about 675K characters) but survived, and T2 searched file names first and scanned with narrower terms. Both passing runs then listed the client's nine matters, read the executed lease and its first-offer exhibit, grepped for first-refusal wording and wrote that the lease grants a first-offer right only. Reviewers' suggested steps were taken as agent-defined stages that fit existing ones; label notes were ignored where they applied.
